rows.selection_reason: No prior experiments exist, so the first step is to establish a baseline. This experiment tests RNA-only modeling with PCA encoding, isolating the effect of the RNA modality and simple encoding. It clarifies whether RNA data alone can achieve reasonable performance, providing foundational evidence for comparing modality importance and encoding choices.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only singleprofile with PCA achieves 0.4849 validation accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with PCA and avgpool aggregation, isolating the effect of profile setting and aggregation. It balances exploration (testing multiprofile) and exploitation (using PCA encoder from baseline), clarifying whether multiprofile improves performance and which aggregation method is effective.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile (config_002) outperforms singleprofile (config_001) with RNA-only models. This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 (config_002) to scvi_n200 while maintaining multiprofile and avgpool aggregation isolates the impact of RNA encoder choice. It balances exploitation of multiprofile's advantage with exploration of a more sophisticated encoder, addressing a key design decision without changing multiple factors simultaneously.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with multiprofile and scvi_n200 encoder (config_005) achieve the highest accuracy (0.650). This experiment tests adding image data (resnet50) with the same RNA encoder and aggregation (avgpool) but using concat fusion, isolating the effect of multimodal inputs. It balances exploitation (building on the best RNA-only model) and exploration (testing image data's impact) without changing multiple factors simultaneously.

Existing evidence shows that rna_only models with scvi_n200 and multiprofile settings achieve higher accuracy (0.65) than multimodal baselines. This experiment tests whether combining scvi_n200 with a stronger image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) and weighted fusion (vs concat in config_030) can improve performance, isolating the impact of image modality and fusion strategy. It balances exploration of multimodal potential with the strong evidence for scvi_n200.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and weighted fusion (config_037) achieve high accuracy (0.706). This experiment tests whether switching aggregation from avgpool (used in config_037) to transformer (a more complex method) further improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation. It builds on the promising multimodal direction while exploring a key design choice (aggregation) that could enhance performance.

Existing evidence shows scvi_n200 (config_005) outperforms pca_n2000 in rna_only/multiprofile setups. This experiment tests whether switching aggregation from avgpool (config_005) to transformer (config_006) further improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It balances exploitation of scvi_n200's strength with exploration of aggregation choices, which are critical for model design.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder with scgpt while keeping the image encoder, aggregation, and fusion consistent. It isolates the impact of RNA encoder choice in the multimodal setting, which is critical for understanding if more advanced encoders improve performance. This is a logical extension of the top-performing configuration and reduces uncertainty about the RNA encoder's role.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder to scgpt while keeping other components identical (transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) could improve performance. It isolates the impact of the RNA encoder choice, which is critical for model design, and explores whether a more advanced encoder (scgpt) can further enhance performance without changing other factors.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion achieves high accuracy (config_039). This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from imagenet_vit_l (used in config_039) with resnet50 affects performance, isolating the impact of the image encoder choice. It balances exploitation of the current high-performing setup with exploration of a simpler image encoder, which may reveal if the choice of image encoder is critical or if resnet50 suffices.
